summary: This bill amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to require more detailed reporting on countries' efforts to combat narcotics-related money laundering, mandates a separate report volume on money laundering issues, and directs the Treasury Secretary to consult with financial agencies to improve consistency in Bank Secrecy Act examinations.

scores.thoughts: This bill amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to improve reporting on international narcotics control and money laundering. While it doesn't directly increase or decrease foreign aid spending, it modifies how certain foreign assistance programs are evaluated and reported, which is a core function of the Foreign Assistance Act. This makes it moderately relevant to the administration of foreign aid.
